department: School for the Environment — Marine Science and Technology PhD

deadline.value: Priority Fall application deadline is March 1, 2027; final Fall deadline is April 1, 2027 (Spring deadline November 1).
deadline.quote: Deadlines: March 1 (priority deadline) and April 1 (final deadline) for fall, November 1 for spring

gre_general.value: GRE test scores are required for Marine Science and Technology PhD admission.
gre_general.quote: Applicants must meet general graduate admission requirements in addition to the following program-specific requirements: | Test Scores: GRE

gre_subject.value: No ETS GRE Subject Test exists for Marine Science and Technology.

also.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: A faculty advisor commitment is required for admission to the Marine Science and Technology PhD program.
supervisor.quote: Applicants must meet general graduate admission requirements in addition to the following program-specific requirements: | Test Scores: GRE | Letters of Recommendation: 2 | Other: Faculty advisor commitment

funding.value: Graduate teaching and research assistantships are assigned by the School for the Environment ($25,865 stipend + 100% tuition waiver for a 1.0 FTE TA/RA in AY 2026-27).
funding.quote: These positions are assigned by the student's department/program and are subject to the agreement between UMass Boston and UAW/Graduate Employees Organization (GEO). | Full Assistantship | 18.00 | 1.00 | $1,293.25 | $25,865.00 | 100%

entry_route.value: Applicants may enter with a bachelor's or master's degree and complete 54 credits; students may earn an en-route MS upon completing core courses and qualifying exams.
entry_route.quote: At the time of enrollment, a bachelor's degree from a regionally accredited U.S. institution of recognized standing or an international equivalent.

also.quote: Complete 54 credits from at least 14 courses including three marine science core courses, one marine policy core course, two School for the Environment seminars, 21 to 22 credits of concentration electives, and 18 credits of dissertation research. | Students may apply to receive a MS in Marine Science and Technology upon completion of all core courses requirements and the written and oral examinations.

notes: Covers physical, chemical, geological, and biological oceanography, marine biogeochemistry, and marine observation technologies.
